question: What governs the skew of RT_out distributions, including the condition under which the exclusion primary dominates over the additive primary or vice versa?

disposition.summary: Skew is governed by the declared statistical projection of imbalance between directed exclusion and addition channels. The bounded asymmetry ratio Omega_a supplies the provisional classifier, but skew appears only after iff_s projection metadata is declared.

provisional_classifier.exclusion_dominant_case: Omega_a > 1 under the declared orientation/sign convention
provisional_classifier.addition_dominant_case: Omega_a < 1 under the declared orientation/sign convention
provisional_classifier.undefined_case: missing orientation convention, missing projection map F_s, missing observation window, missing normalization policy, or failed admissibility trace

skew_reading.balanced: No directional skew is licensed by the classifier alone; any observed skew must come from projection metadata or unresolved heterogeneity.
skew_reading.exclusion_dominant: Tail suppression, truncation, or left/right bias may be projected depending on the declared orientation of the exclusion channel.
skew_reading.addition_dominant: Accumulation, tail extension, or opposite bias may be projected depending on the declared orientation of the addition channel.

required_metadata: orientation/sign convention for exclusion versus addition
bounded asymmetry ratio or equivalent imbalance metric
failure class for mixed or non-equivalent regimes
failure_conditions: Omega_a is used without declared direction order.
Skew is inferred directly from RT_core.
A distribution shape is asserted before iff_s projection metadata is supplied.
Mixed regimes are aggregated without equivalence rules.
The sign of skew is treated as orientation-independent.
Observed skew is treated as proof of exclusion or addition dominance without an admissible trace.

relationship_to_oq_002.note: Bell-curve derivability requires projection conditions. OQ_003 supplies the complementary non-symmetric shape classifier for cases where those conditions do not force an unskewed normal-like output.

remaining_work: Define the signed skew projection function under F_s.
Specify whether skew sign follows exclusion channel orientation or observation-axis orientation.
Construct positive and negative skew examples under declared metadata.
Harden compatibility with L124 and P118 bounded Omega_a rules.

does_not_prove: A theorem deriving skew from RT_core.
An empirical or physical distribution claim.
